gaps.sentence: The ___ traffic added an hour to our journey.
gaps.explanation: heavy traffic means a lot of vehicles on the road; 'thick traffic' is not standard.

gaps.sentence: We ___ the risk of flooding very seriously.
gaps.explanation: 'Take something seriously' is the fixed phrase.

gaps.sentence: He ___ a fortune by buying his train ticket in advance.
gaps.explanation: save a fortune means to avoid spending a large amount; buying in advance keeps money.

gaps.sentence: Even after she moved abroad, we ___ in touch by email.
gaps.explanation: keep in touch means to maintain contact with someone.

gaps.sentence: Most children learn to ___ the time before they start school.
gaps.hint: fixed phrase: ___ the time (read a clock)
gaps.explanation: tell the time means to be able to read a clock; it is a fixed expression.

gaps.sentence: Make sure you are fully ___ of the terms before you sign.
gaps.explanation: fully aware of something is the fixed collocation meaning knowing completely.

gaps.sentence: Who ___ the washing-up in your house?
gaps.explanation: do the washing-up means to wash the dishes; the -s form is needed with 'who'.

gaps.sentence: He didn't ___ any interest in politics until university.
gaps.explanation: take an interest in something means to become curious or involved in it.
